source.how: get_computed_styles for the declared values; get_node_info / get_children for the laid-out rects, whose world coordinates are what `gaps` is computed from.

note: Three figures, one inside the next. Paper draws the toast as ONE padded, bordered node; the render splits it — a bordered shell around a padded content row — because Base UI's stack clamps the shell's height to the frontmost toast and the row is what overflow-hides. The union arithmetic is identical: the sheet's 17px inset is the shell's 1px used border plus the row's 16px padding, asserted here as 1 and 16 on their own containers. The content row is the load-bearing case: four fixed slots and one flexing text column, where the vertical gaps are read off the UNION of center-aligned children of four different heights — the text column (62) is the tallest, so it alone touches the padding box.

lawsNotDeclared.concentric-radius: The content row carries no radius of its own — it is clipped by the shell's radius-lg via overflow-hidden, which is the stack's height clamp doing its job. An unpainted radius is not a fact about the design.

The trailing controls' radii belong to their own primitives — the Action is Button md (radius-md, 8) and the Close hit area is radius-sm (4) — and both sit a full 16px padding inside the shell's corner, where concentricity would demand radius 0.
Neither the column nor its text lines paints a fill, a border or a corner — an unpainted radius is not a fact about the design.

deviations.what: Paper draws padding and border on one node (its toast root is a single 416×96 padded frame); the render splits them across the shell and the content row.
deviations.why: Base UI clamps the shell's height to the frontmost toast while the stack is collapsed and the content row is what overflow-hides — sizing the row to the shell would cancel the height transition (Base UI's own varying-heights note). The sheet's 17px inset is asserted as the sum of the two cases: the shell's 1px used border plus the row's 16px padding.

deviations.what: The sheet's children are center-aligned in a row set by the tallest child, so per-child vertical offsets differ (icon at 16, action at 31, close at 35); only the union of the four rects is asserted against the padding box. The icon slot renders one title line tall (1lh ≈ 21.6) where Paper rounds it to 22, and the text/action widths are what this specimen's strings produced.
deviations.why: align-items: center is the design: fixed-height controls float on the cross axis while the text column defines it — any child taller than the text column would surface as a broken vertical gap. The text column is the single flexing slot (flex: 1, min-width: 0), so its width, and therefore the action's neighbourly position, moves with the copy and the window; the law's horizontal arithmetic binds whatever they measure.

deviations.what: The sheet reports the title line as 22 tall and the two wrapped description lines as 36; Chromium's line boxes are 21.6 and 35.1 at the same tokens.
deviations.why: Paper rounds text node heights to whole pixels. Nothing asserts the absolute line heights — the case exists for the 4px gap between them, which both sides agree on.
